text_blocks.snippet: The immune system's response to COVID-19 is a complex, multi-phased process involving both innate and adaptive immune responses. Initially, innate immune cells like natural killer (NK) cells and macrophages are activated to clear infected cells and produce cytokines. The adaptive immune system then kicks in, with T cells and B cells responding to the viral antigens, leading to the production of neutralizing antibodies and the development of long-term immune memory.

list.title: Immediate Response:
list.snippet: When the virus enters the body, innate immune cells like NK cells and macrophages are rapidly activated.

list.title: Cell Killing:
list.snippet: NK cells directly attack and destroy infected cells that harbor the virus.

list.title: Antigen Presentation:
list.snippet: Macrophages engulf the virus, break it down, and present viral antigens on their surface, signaling the start of the adaptive immune response.

list.title: Cytokine Production:
list.snippet: Both NK cells and macrophages release cytokines, which are signaling molecules that help recruit other immune cells and coordinate the overall immune response.

list.title: T Cell Activation:
list.snippet: T cells, including helper T cells and cytotoxic T cells, are activated by the presented antigens.

list.title: B Cell Activation:
list.snippet: Helper T cells stimulate B cells to produce antibodies.

list.title: Antibody Production:
list.snippet: B cells differentiate into plasma cells, which produce antibodies that bind to the virus and neutralize it, preventing it from infecting new cells.

list.title: Immune Memory:
list.snippet: Some T cells and B cells become memory cells, providing long-term immunity and a quicker response upon re-exposure to the virus.

list.title: Individual Variability:
list.snippet: The effectiveness of the immune response can vary greatly among individuals, depending on factors like age, genetics, and overall health.

list.title: Viral Strain:
list.snippet: Different variants of the virus may trigger slightly different immune responses.

list.title: Prior Exposure:
list.snippet: Prior exposure to related viruses or vaccinations can influence the speed and strength of the immune response.
